<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIIII.|TO THE ROMANES.|417}}</noinclude>Lord. And he that eateth, eateth to our Lord: for he giueth thankes to God. And he that eateth not, to our Lord he eateth not, and giueth thankes to God. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=7}}† For none of vs liueth to him self: & no man dieth to him self. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=8}}† For whether vve liue, we liue to our Lord: or vvhether we die, we die to our Lord. Therfore vvhether vve liue, or vvhether vve die, vve are our Lords. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=9}}† For to this end Christ died and rose againe: that he may haue dominion both of the dead and of the liuing. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=10}}† But thou, vvhy iudgest thou thy brother? or thou, vvhy doest thou despise thy brother? For {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''2. Cor. 5, 10.''}}* vve shal al stand before the iudgement seate of Christ. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=11}}† For it is vvritten, ''Liue I'', saith our Lord, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 45, 23.''}}* ''that euery knee shal bovve to me: and euery tongue shal confesse to God''. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=12}}† Therfore euery one of vs for him self shal render account to God. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=13}}† Let vs therfore no more iudge one an other. but this iudge ye rather, that you put not a stumbling blocke or a scandal to your brother. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=14}}† I knovv and am persuaded in our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} Christ, that nothing is {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Common'', that is, ''vncleane''. See Annot. Marc. ''7, 2''.}}∷ common of it self, but to him that supposeth, any thing to be common, to him it is common. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Cor. 8.''}}* For if because of meate thy brother be greeued: novv thou vvalkest not according to charitie. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Though he vvish the vveake to be borne withal, yet he vttereth his minde plainly, that in deede al the meates forbidden and vncleane in the Law, are now through Christ cleansed & lawful for euery man to vse.}}∷ Do not vvith thy meate destroy him for vvhom Christ died. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=16}}† Let not then our good be blasphemed. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=17}}† For the kingdom of God is {{sup|‖}} not meate and drinke: but iustice, and peace, and ioy in the holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=18}}† For he that in this serueth Christ, pleaseth God, and is acceptable to men. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=19}}† Therfore the things that are of peace let vs pursue: and the things that are of edifying one tovvard an other let vs keepe. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=20}}† Destroy not the vvorke of God for meate. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Tit. 1, 15.''}}* Al things in deede are cleane: but it is il for the man that eateth by giuing offence. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=21}}† It is good not to eate flesh, and not to drinke vvine, nor that vvherein thy brother is offended, or scandalized, or vveakened. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=22}}† Hast thou faith? {{sup|‖}} haue it vvith thy self before God. Blessed is he that iudgeth not him self in that vvhich he approueth. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=23}}† But {{sup|‖}} he that discerneth, if he eate, is damned: because not of faith. for {{sup|‖}} al that is not of faith, is sinne.
